chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn Uthman said:
A man came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and complained to him about a man from his companions. It was not long before the one complained against came.
So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What is the matter so-and-so is complaining against you?' So he said to him: 'He complains about me that I collected my right from him'.
He said, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sat up in anger, then said: 'It is as if when you collected your right, you did not offend'.
They are fearing the evil Reckoning
Do you see that they feared Allah that He would be inequitable to them? No, by Allah! They did not fear except for the collection (of debts), so Allah Mighty and Majestic named it the evil Reckoning.
So the one who collects by it, he has offended.

key_terms.أَسَاءَ: He did wrong/offended, indicating a failure in ethical conduct or social etiquette.
key_terms.أَصْحَابِهِ: His companions, referring to the community of followers or peers of the Imam.
key_terms.الاسْتِقْضَاءُ: The act of collecting a debt or right from another person, often implying a formal or public demand.
key_terms.سُوءَ الْحِسَابِ: Evil Reckoning or bad accounting, referring to the Quranic phrase indicating a source of blame or negative consequence.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of 'istiqda'' (collecting debt) in Shia ethics according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates the act of *istiqda'* (collecting debt from a peer) from a mere legal right to an ethical shortcoming, linking it to the Quranic concept of 'evil Reckoning' (Su' al-Hisab). This reflects the Shia emphasis on *adab al-mu'amalat* (etiquette of dealings), where preserving social harmony and avoiding the appearance of injustice often outweighs strict legal entitlement. The Imam’s anger underscores the gravity of this practice, suggesting that while one has the right to collect, the manner and context can render it a source of spiritual blame.
